caption:
Persistent thermal monitoring flags heat anomalies — illegal refining sites, flaring, fire fronts — against a baseline of normal activity for that terrain. It does this well. What it does not do is tell you, on its own, what is burning or who lit it.

A thermal return is a cue, not a conclusion. It says: this pixel is hotter than its history. It does not say: this is a cook site versus a bush fire versus a flare stack venting on schedule. That identification takes corroboration — optical imagery, radar, ground reporting — before a patrol gets tasked.

And like every pass-based sensor, thermal monitoring only sees the moment it looks. A burn that starts and ends between revisits leaves no signature. The system reports what it observed, when it observed it — not a continuous watch over the area.

State the limit with the finding. That is what makes the finding usable.
thread: Persistent thermal monitoring flags heat anomalies against a site's normal pattern. It does not tell you what's burning or who lit it. That's the limit — and it's the part worth stating out loud.
A thermal return is a cue, not a conclusion. Cook site, bush fire, flare stack venting on schedule — all read as heat. Identification needs corroboration before anyone gets tasked to respond.
Thermal monitoring is also pass-based like everything else in the collection plan. A short burn between revisits leaves no trace. The report covers what was observed, when — not a continuous watch.
A cue that overstates its own certainty costs the same as a false alarm: a dispatched patrol for nothing. Grade the confidence, name the gap, let the responder decide.

card.headline: A heat flag names a hotspot, not a cause
card.sub: Thermal monitoring detects anomalies against baseline. It does not identify the source — that takes corroboration before anyone is tasked to respond.

rationale: Introduces a capability not yet covered (thermal anomaly detection) while reinforcing the series' core discipline of stating limits plainly, without repeating prior angles' phrasing or examples.
